newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan shuts zoo to "protect animals from humans".
newsitem.headline: Taiwan shuts zoo to "protect animals from humans".

text.p: Taiwan's capital on Tuesday shut its zoo for 12 days to protect its animals from the most likely carriers of a deadly hog epidemic -- humans.
"We are not protecting the people from the animals. Rather, we are protecting the animals from the people," a Taipei Zoo spokesman said by telephone.
The zoo said it would vaccinate all of its 2,000-plus animals during the shutdown amid an outbreak of highly contagious foot-and-mouth disease on the island's hog farms.
"Humans cannot become ill from foot and mouth disease but can easily spread the virus to vulnerable animals, especially cloven-hoofed animals," the spokesman said.
In a massive eradication drive, Taiwan already has begun destroying nearly 400,000 of Taiwan's 10 million hogs on 357 infected farms.
The spokesman said the zoo had to exercise extreme caution because most visitors come from southern Taiwan, where the outbreak was most concentrated.

The hog epidemic has sparked a total ban on pork exports and an army-led eradication drive that have battered the stock market, threatened thousands of layoffs and handed a new setback to Taiwan's gathering economic recovery.
